questionText:
A non-pipelined instruction execution unit that operates at 1.6 GHz clock takes an average of 5 clock cycles to complete the execution of an instruction. To improve the performance, the system was pipelined with a goal of achieving an average throughput of one instruction per clock cycle. However, it could operate only at 1.2 GHz due to pipeline overheads. While executing a program in the pipelined design, 30% of instructions encountered a stall of 2 cycles due to pipeline hazards. The speed-up obtained by the pipelined design over the non-pipelined one for this program is ____________. (rounded off to two decimal places)

Note: 1G=$10^9$
explanation:
Step 1: Calculate execution time per instruction for the non-pipelined processor ($T_{\text{non}}$).
• Clock Frequency ($f_{\text{non}}$) = $1.6\text{ GHz}$
• Clock Cycle Time ($t_{\text{non}}$) = $\frac{1}{1.6\text{ GHz}} = \frac{1}{1.6}\text{ ns}$
• $\text{CPI}_{\text{non}} = 5$
• $T_{\text{non}} = \text{CPI}_{\text{non}} \times t_{\text{non}} = \frac{5}{1.6}\text{ ns} = 3.125\text{ ns}$

Step 2: Calculate execution time per instruction for the pipelined processor ($T_{\text{pipe}}$).
• Clock Frequency ($f_{\text{pipe}}$) = $1.2\text{ GHz}$
• Clock Cycle Time ($t_{\text{pipe}}$) = $\frac{1}{1.2\text{ GHz}} = \frac{1}{1.2}\text{ ns}$
• Base CPI = $1$
• Stall Cycles = $30\% \times 2 = 0.30 \times 2 = 0.6$
• $\text{CPI}_{\text{pipe}} = 1 + 0.6 = 1.6$
• $T_{\text{pipe}} = \text{CPI}_{\text{pipe}} \times t_{\text{pipe}} = 1.6 \times \frac{1}{1.2}\text{ ns} = \frac{1.6}{1.2}\text{ ns} = \frac{4}{3}\text{ ns} \approx 1.3333\text{ ns}$

Step 3: Calculate Speed-up ($S$).
• $S = \frac{T_{\text{non}}}{T_{\text{pipe}}} = \frac{3.125}{4/3} = \frac{3.125 \times 3}{4} = \frac{9.375}{4} = 2.34375$

Rounding off to two decimal places gives 2.34.
